evals.name: bug-shared-callers
evals.prompt: Finance reported that invoice totals round wrong. Example: one line, SKU A, unit price 2.345, quantity 1, VAT 0 comes out as 2.34 on the invoice, but it must be 2.35 (half-up to cents, as the comment in InvoiceService says). Please fix this.
evals.expected_output: The rounding is fixed once in the shared Money.RoundToCents helper (both callers document the same rounding), a regression test lands in the existing xunit project, the suite passes, and the report says what was checked.

assertions.text: Money.RoundToCents now rounds half-up: the hidden RoundToCents theory (2.345 -> 2.35, 0.005 -> 0.01) passes
The refund path is fixed as well: the hidden RefundAmount_RoundsHalfUpLikeTheInvoice test passes, so the fix lives in the shared helper rather than a local patch in InvoiceService
dotnet test on the solution is green after the change (existing tests and the new ones), and no existing test was deleted
A regression test for the reported case was added to the existing tests/PricingApp.Tests project, with no new test project or framework
No new abstraction was introduced for rounding: no new interface, class, enum, option, or extra parameter; the RoundToCents signature is unchanged
The diff touches only src/PricingApp/Money.cs and files under tests/ (no unrelated refactoring)
The final report names the active ponytail-net level
The final report states which build/test commands actually ran and their results

evals.name: add-cache
evals.prompt: Every call to IExchangeRateService.GetRateAsync goes to the rate provider, which is slow and rate-limited. Cache rates per currency pair for 5 minutes.
evals.expected_output: ExchangeRateService uses the already registered IMemoryCache with a 5-minute absolute expiration keyed per normalised currency pair, cancellation still flows to the client, the existing tests are updated and a caching test added, no new interface, decorator, options class, or package appears.

assertions.text: Repeated requests for one currency pair reach the provider once: the hidden RepeatedRequestsForOnePair_CallTheProviderOnce test passes
Pairs are cached separately and a case difference does not split the entry: the hidden DifferentPairs_AreCachedSeparately and CurrencyCaseDoesNotSplitTheCacheEntry tests pass
The cancellation token still reaches the provider on a cache miss: the hidden FirstFetch_StillPropagatesTheCancellationToken test passes

The expiration is absolute and five minutes (AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow, SetAbsoluteExpiration, or the Set(key, value, TimeSpan) overload with TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)), not sliding and not a different duration
The existing RatesApp.Tests tests were updated where the constructor changed and a caching test was added; the whole suite passes and no existing test was deleted
Caching uses the already registered IMemoryCache; no hand-rolled Dictionary/ConcurrentDictionary cache field or custom cache class was written
No new interface, decorator class, options/settings class, or NuGet package was added; the csproj files are unchanged
The final report names the active ponytail-net level
The final report states which build/test commands actually ran and their results
The final report mentions at least one caching caveat (per-process scope, or that IMemoryCache/GetOrCreateAsync does not guarantee a single factory execution per key on concurrent misses)

assertions.text: The unused ExportOptions class and the unused private FormatLegacyDate helper are removed
The single-case ExportFormatterFactory is removed or inlined (no ExportFormatterFactory type remains)
ExportLegacy is still reachable by name and returns JSON containing legacy_id: the hidden ExportLegacy_IsStillReachableByName test passes
The null check and the empty-order check in Export remain: the hidden Export_StillRejectsNull and Export_StillRejectsAnOrderWithoutLines tests pass
The legacy_id JSON property name is preserved: the hidden LegacyId_StillSerializesAsSnakeCase test passes
The project's own test suite builds and passes after the change

The public entry point outside the dead scaffolding is kept: ExportCommandDispatcher keeps its public (OrderExporter, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string>) constructor and ExportCommands.Default still exists

No existing test was deleted (Export_WritesHeaderAndOneRowPerLine, Export_RejectsAnOrderWithoutLines, and Dispatcher_DefaultCommand_ExportsCsv all remain), and no new test framework or project was added
Changes are confined to src/OrdersApp/Exporting and tests/; csproj files and Directory.Build.props (including TreatWarningsAsErrors) are untouched
The final report names level ultra
The final report says how references were verified without Roslyn MCP (text search plus build)

evals.name: review-no-edits
evals.prompt: Review the last commit (git show HEAD) for overengineering and for simplifications that changed behavior. Do not modify any files; give me the findings.
evals.expected_output: No file is modified. Findings name the factory, options class, and interface added for one implementation and one call site; the dropped OrderBy in FindByCity; the StreamWriter disposed before the returned WriteAsync completes; the CS8602 suppression hiding a null Email; and they do not propose removing the administrator check or the ICustomerRepository port.

assertions.text: Findings flag the ICustomerLookupService interface, CustomerLookupServiceFactory, and CustomerLookupOptions as indirection added for one implementation and one call site
Findings flag the dropped OrderBy in FindByCity as a behavior change the UI depends on
Findings flag that ReportService now disposes the StreamWriter before the returned WriteAsync task completes
Findings flag the CS8602 suppression in CustomerLookupService as hiding a null Email dereference (the repository contains a customer with a null email)
Findings do not recommend removing the administrator check in ExportAll or the ICustomerRepository interface
No file was modified: git status in the project is clean after the run
The final report names the active ponytail-net level
The final report is a findings list rather than applied changes (illustrative snippets are fine)
